author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty. Matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case. With no specialty named, both forms behave as they do today.
acceptance_criteria: the paged veterinarian page accepts an optional specialty parameter and lists only veterinarians holding that specialty
the machine-readable veterinarian list accepts the same optional specialty parameter and returns only those veterinarians
matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; a name that is only the beginning of a stored specialty matches no veterinarian
a specialty no veterinarian holds yields the normal page or document with an empty veterinarian list and a success status
an empty or spaces-only specialty behaves as if no specialty had been named, and the whole directory is returned
a specialty with leading or trailing spaces matches the same specialty without them
paging links on a narrowed page carry the named specialty, so later pages stay narrowed
with no specialty named, both forms return exactly what they return today
non_goals: any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing the specialty on either form of the directory
narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
narrowing the owner, pet, or visit surfaces
notes: Open points resolved by the narrowest reading, per the owner's standing instruction that no further product answer will come. (1) One requirement, not two: the owner asked to mint one fresh requirement, so REQ-VET-003 carries both the reinstated machine-readable surface and the narrowing; REQ-VET-004 was not minted. Recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md. (2) A specialty with surrounding spaces is trimmed before matching, following REQ-OWN-002, which the owner named as the precedent. Recorded as edge case 3 and as an open question. (3) The Superseded entry for REQ-VET-002 keeps the withdrawal and drops 'pending removal'; the route is a supported surface again under REQ-VET-003. The Veterinarian directory known-defect edge case about the second route is removed, since the route now carries a requirement. (4) The NG-9 narrowing is recorded as a non-goal ADR alongside the table edit, matching the 2026-08-08 NG-4 and NG-5 precedent: docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-vet-search-narrowed.md. Two files outside my write scope still need the same change and are for system-design-expert: docs/system-design.md's known-defect row saying the machine-readable route serves no requirement, and the ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md for the new non-goal ADR. Page size for the vet list is a local variable today (docs/system-design.md#constants notes it); narrowing must not change the page size.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing stays inside the vet feature package and adds no module, layer, or dependency: VetController keeps calling VetRepository directly, per the feature-package-without-a-service-layer ADR. Two design points were genuinely new ground and are now recorded in docs/system-design.md (Contracts, Threat Model) behind docs/adr/2026-08-15-vet-directory-narrowing-as-uncached-query.md. First, the narrowing is a repository query applied before paging, stating case-insensitive whole-name matching in the query itself rather than inheriting it from a vendor collation, so the PostgreSQL divergence recorded as a Known Defect against REQ-OWN-002 is not repeated. Second, the narrowed lookups stay outside the vets cache, which is Caffeine-backed with no size limit and no eviction, so no caller-supplied string reaches a cache key. The two existing unnarrowed read methods keep their @Cacheable annotations unchanged. Blank handling follows OwnerController.processFindForm, which strips the submitted last name and treats the empty string as the broadest search. Basis for the covering-pattern claims is grep over the vet and owner packages plus a direct read of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, VetControllerTests, CacheConfiguration, vetList.html and build.gradle; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two declared query methods over the Vet-to-Specialty association: one paged for /vets.html and one unpaged returning a Collection for /vets. The interface extends the bare Repository marker, so only declared methods exist and nothing else changes.

VetController.showVetList and VetController.showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty request parameter. Both normalize it before use: strip surrounding spaces, then treat blank as absent and take the existing unnarrowed path.
VetController.addPaginationModel adds the normalized specialty to the model so vetList.html can carry it on paging links. The attribute is absent, not empty, when no specialty was named.

vetList.html builds its six paging links as Thymeleaf link expressions with named parameters instead of the current string concatenation, so the specialty is URL-encoded and a null specialty omits the parameter entirely.
Vets, the serialization wrapper for the /vets route, now serves REQ-VET-003 and its Contracts row moved off the em-dash marker.

patterns.description: processFindForm: the precedent for normalizing an optional search parameter — strip the value, treat the empty string as the broadest search, then page the result. The PRD names REQ-OWN-002 as the precedent for trimming.
findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable): the derived paged query pattern the narrowed vet query follows.
addPaginationModel and findPaginated: the existing pagination helper pair the narrowing threads through. Page size stays the local variable it is today.

risks.risk: Copying @Cacheable("vets") onto the narrowed query methods by symmetry with the two existing read methods. The cache has no size limit and no eviction, and the key would carry an unauthenticated caller's string, so the cache could be grown without bound.
risks.mitigation: The narrowed lookups carry no cache annotation. Recorded in docs/system-design.md Contracts and Threat Model, behind the ADR.

risks.risk: Relying on the database collation for case-insensitive matching, as owner search does. That reproduces the recorded PostgreSQL divergence on the vendors whose collation is case-sensitive.
risks.mitigation: State case-insensitivity in the query itself so every vendor matches alike. The H2-backed suite cannot observe a vendor divergence, so the query text is the guarantee, not the test.

risks.risk: Filtering the fetched page in the controller instead of in the query. Pages would be short and the page count would describe the unnarrowed directory, so the paging acceptance criterion would fail intermittently rather than outright.
risks.mitigation: The narrowing is a repository query; paging applies to the narrowed selection. Assert the total page count on a narrowed multi-page result, not only the row contents.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is an EAGER ManyToMany. A paged query that joins the association can degrade to in-memory paging in Hibernate, which passes the tests while reading the whole table.
risks.mitigation: Match on the association in the where clause rather than with a fetch join. Watch the build log for Hibernate's in-memory-pagination warning during the Refactor step.

risks.risk: Building the paging hrefs by concatenating the specialty into the existing @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} string. An ampersand or hash in the specialty truncates the link, and the value is caller-supplied.
risks.mitigation: Use link-expression parameters, which URL-encode each value and omit a null parameter. Cover with a specialty containing a space.

risks.risk: Changing the vet page size while touching the pagination helper. The page size is a local variable, not a named constant, and REQ-VET-001's existing behavior depends on it.
risks.mitigation: Leave the local variable untouched; the unnarrowed acceptance criterion asserts today's output exactly.

notes: Design-level open points, resolved by the narrowest reading per the owner's standing instruction and recorded here rather than raised. (1) Caching the narrowed lookups: not cached — the requirement asks for narrowing, not for cached narrowing, and the unnarrowed cache that REQ-VET-001 relies on is untouched. Recorded in the ADR. (2) Where case-insensitivity is stated: in the query, not the collation. Recorded in the ADR. (3) Whether the machine-readable route gains paging: no — the requirement narrows it and says nothing about paging, so it keeps returning the whole narrowed collection. (4) Whether the narrowed page shows the reader which specialty is active: no — a visible indication is the page control the intake excluded, so the specialty appears only in the links. Open for the follow-up request that adds a control. (5) Whether an unknown specialty is distinguishable from one no veterinarian holds: no — both yield the normal page with an empty list, as the acceptance criteria require. Follow-ups outside the product expert's write scope, both now done: the Known Defects row saying the machine-readable route serves no requirement is removed from docs/system-design.md, and docs/adr/README.md gained index rows for both 2026-08-15 ADRs — the non-goal ADR row was missing entirely, not only unindexed for the new one. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain note, not a defect in this change: the OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, so dependencyCheckAnalyze did not run and no NVD match was performed in this review. The change adds no dependency, so the resolved set is the pre-existing baseline and the gap is not attributable here — but the NVD check on Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its transitive Jackson remains not verified and should be closed by CI or a human, not assumed clean.

The UPPER(specialty.name) = UPPER(:specialty) predicate defeats any index on specialty.name, so each narrowed request is a scan of the specialties join. At the seeded directory's size this is immaterial and it is not a security finding; if the directory ever grows to a size where an unauthenticated GET can be repeated cheaply for load, a functional index or a normalized stored column would remove the amplification.
approved_aspects: Data-access injection: both new VetRepository.findBySpecialtyName overloads use a static @Query with a named :specialty bound through @Param. No request-derived value is concatenated into query text; the JPQL string is assembled from compile-time literals only. Passes docs/security-principles.md Realization row 'Injection into data access'.

XSS: the caller-supplied specialty never reaches the DOM as markup. vetList.html renders it only inside @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} link expressions, where Thymeleaf URL-encodes the parameter value and then HTML-escapes the attribute. Grep of src/main/resources/templates confirms no th:utext and no __${...}__ preprocessing anywhere; the change in fact removes the six pre-existing __${...}__ paging expressions (previously int-valued, so no exploit, but the safer construct now stands). Passes 'Cross-site scripting'.

Cache poisoning / unbounded cache growth avoided: the narrowed queries deliberately carry no @Cacheable, so a caller-supplied specialty cannot become an unevictable key in the size-unlimited 'vets' cache. Rationale is recorded inline and in docs/adr/2026-08-15-vet-directory-narrowing-as-uncached-query.md. This is the fail-secure choice, not merely the performant one.

Boundary normalization: VetController.namedSpecialtyOf strips and maps blank to null at the controller boundary, matching OwnerController.processFindForm's reading of an empty search box. Defensive handling sits at the boundary, not scattered inward, per the brief's 'Internal code, past the boundary, trusts its contracts'.
Exposed surface: no new endpoint. /vets.html and /vets each gain one optional @RequestParam; no management endpoint exposure changes, no new mutating route. Passes 'Widening the exposed surface'.

Mass assignment: the two new inputs are scalar @RequestParam values (int page, String specialty). No new request-bound command type, so no identifier-binding disallow list is owed. Passes 'Mass assignment'.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Eleven files inside one feature package plus its docs: two GET endpoints gain an optional parameter, VetRepository gains two query methods, and vetList.html's six paging links are rewritten from concatenated query strings into link expressions. No sensitive path, one module, and the unnarrowed page's rendered hrefs come out unchanged and are regression-asserted.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading every hunk found nothing at odds with the stated change: the EXISTS subquery narrows before paging so the page count describes the narrowed selection, UPPER on both sides states case-insensitivity in the query rather than inheriting a vendor collation, and a blank value maps to null so the unnarrowed path stays byte-identical. The two asymmetries are deliberate and ADR-recorded - narrowed lookups stay outside the unbounded vets cache, and a narrowed single-page result shows no sign of its narrowing because totalPages > 1 gates the only place the specialty is echoed.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise the changed behavior against reality rather than restating it: ClinicServiceTests drives real H2 for case-insensitive matching, partial-name non-matching, and a totalElements of 2 that would read 6 if paging preceded narrowing; VetControllerTests asserts the rendered hrefs including the URL-encoded space and asserts an unnarrowed page carries no specialty= at all. Each would fail against a plausibly broken implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved with empty findings, but the security-reviewer's round-2 approval carries two recommendations forward unresolved - OWASP Dependency-Check is still unconfigured so no NVD match ran against Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its transitive Jackson, and UPPER(specialty.name) defeats any index on the specialties join reached by an unauthenticated GET - and the implementer's build-pass note parks those two plus the code-quality reviewer's template fragment-extraction note explicitly for the human.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the recorded intake decisions line for line: a URL contract only with no form or dropdown on either surface, NG-9 narrowed through its own ADR on the 2026-08-08 precedent, and a fresh REQ-VET-003 with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn and its id unreused. The single design revision only added docs/adr/README.md to the record's supporting paths; no consultation and no build retry.

rationale: The code is clean and the tests are real; nothing in the diff needs rework. What needs a human is the residual the reviewers parked: no NVD scan has ever run against this dependency set, and the narrowed query scans an unindexed join on an unauthenticated GET. Accept or ticket both.
